text:
maria-g: heads up — seeing sporadic 1–3ms tail spikes on L4 when the runtime flips kernel paths based on SM capability. small-batch, latency-sensitive traffic only. any ideas? :thinking:
ashwin: saw similar traces last week on a canary. looks like a race between the scheduler and the kernel-switch path. kernel switch launches a prep kernel then the real kernel — occasional double-launch + teardown cost.
tj: can you paste a log snippet?
maria-g: sure — snippet from runtime.log:
```
[2024-11-12T08:02:11Z] device=nvL4 idx=2 capability_mask=0x7 -> choosing path=SIMD_FALLBACK
[2024-11-12T08:02:11Z] device=nvL4 idx=2 launch=prep_kernel id=0xabc
[2024-11-12T08:02:11Z] device=nvL4 idx=2 scheduler->assign kernel_id=0xdef
[2024-11-12T08:02:11Z] device=nvL4 idx=2 launch=prep_kernel id=0xabc (duplicate)
[2024-11-12T08:02:11Z] kernel_switch_duration_ms=2.8
```
selena: ugh — duplicate prep launches. i think the scheduler retries if it doesn't see an ack inside 50ms; but the prep path doesn't ack early enough for tiny batches.
perf-bot: metric alert — latency_p50: 1.8ms, latency_p99 spike to +2.9ms correlated with kernel_switch_count on nvL4 nodes.
ashwin: root cause hypothesis: no tight in-flight guard for per-device kernel-switch. scheduler and runtime both try to be resilient -> retries. on hw with fast prep cost (L4), retries cost proportionally more to tiny batches.
yuki: alternatives we discussed: 1) central coordinator (single sequencer) to serialize switches, 2) per-device semaphore/handshake to ensure single in-flight switch, 3) speculative launches with a cheap kill path, 4) increase ack timeouts.
maria-g: central sequencer is heavy and adds RTT; not ideal for Dedicated/Private. increasing timeout just delays. speculative kill seems risky (we already have resource pressure).
ashwin: leaning to a per-device handshake plus an optimistic local cache — runtime exposes `capability_change_inflight` boolean and returns `ACK` immediately once prep queued. scheduler checks that flag and won't launch another prep if set. if no ACK within X ms, scheduler will backoff with exponential jitter. simple state machine.
tj: tradeoffs?
ashwin: low complexity, no cross-host coord, low-latency for common case. needs careful atomicity on the runtime side and some GC for stale flags (device crash). needs telemetry tags to debug.
selena: can we also emit a small telemetry event when duplicate-prep detected, with stack id + device id? that'll speed root-cause.
yuki: agree. add `kernel_switch_dup` counter + sample a single trace payload per minute.
maria-g: plan proposal: ashwin implements handshake flag + immediate ACK path; yuki adds dup counters and sampled trace; selena updates scheduler to check flag + exponential backoff (initial 5ms, cap 200ms); canary rollout to 0.5% of L4 traffic, mirrored on H100 to validate behavior there.
ashwin: implement notes: atomic compare-and-set at runtime for `inflight_flag`; ACK includes a small token id string. scheduler stores token and only clears on explicit DONE/FAIL or on token timeout. use device-local monotonic clock for timeout.
perf-bot: suggested canary config: sample_rate=0.005, max_concurrent_canaries=10, duration=2h.
selena: i'll add the scheduler change. ashwin — want to pair on the test harness?
ashwin: yes, DM to schedule pairing.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled for cluster=staging-l4 at 2024-11-14T22:00Z with config {"sample_rate":"0.005","duration":"2h"} :rocket:
maria-g: thanks everyone — follow-ups: ashwin PR with handshake proto, yuki telemetry PR, selena scheduler PR. we'll reconvene after canary window to decide if we need stronger invariant (central sequencer) or if this is sufficient. :thumbsup:
